questions.question: If 16 cot A = 12, then find the value of (sin A + cos A)/(sin A - cos A)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given: 16 cot A = 12 ⇒ cot A = 12/16 = 3/4

Expression to find: (sin A + cos A) ÷ (sin A − cos A)

Divide numerator and denominator by sin A:

⇒ (1 + cot A) ÷ (1 − cot A)

⇒ (1 + 3/4) ÷ (1 − 3/4) = (7/4) ÷ (1/4) = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

16 cot A = 12 ⇒ cot A = 3/4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd9e31f32080ba34afee57f46856b07d15b2af374772668bbcba5b2fad76584c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

sin A = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

cos A = Base ÷ Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

⇒ cot A = Base ÷ Perpendicular = 3/4

⇒ Let Base = 3x and Perpendicular = 4x

⇒ Hypotenuse = √((3x)² + (4x)²)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(9x² + 16x²) = √(25x²) = 5x

⇒ sin A = 4x ÷ 5x = 4/5

⇒ cos A = 3x ÷ 5x = 3/5

Now, substitute the values in the expression: (sin A + cos A) ÷ (sin A − cos A)

⇒ (4/5 + 3/5) ÷ (4/5 − 3/5)

⇒ (7/5) ÷ (1/5) = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Definitions

In a right-angled triangle, tan A = sin A ÷ cos A = Perpendicular ÷ Base, and cot A = cos A ÷ sin A = Base ÷ Perpendicular.

Pythagorean Triples

Common integer sets satisfying Pythagoras theorem include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17) and (7, 24, 25). These combinations save critical calculation time in exams.

Key Trigonometric Identities

Basic square identities are: sin² A + cos² A = 1, 1 + tan² A = sec² A, and 1 + cot² A = cosec² A.

questions.question: A bus covers a distance of 5 km in 20 min. If its speed is decreased by 3 km/hr, then find the time taken by the bus to cover the same distance.

Distance covered in 20 minutes by the bus = 5 km

Speed = Distance/Time

Initial speed of the bus = 5 km/ 20 minutes 

⇒ 5 km/ 20 × 60

After reduction in speed, 

Time = 5 km/(15 km/h - 3 km/h) 

⇒ 5/12 hours

questions.question: How long will it take a sum of money invested at 6% p.a. on simple interest to increase its value by 50%?
questions.solution:

Rate of simple interest = 6% p.a. 

**Formula used:**

Amount = Principal + Simple interest 

Simple Interest = Principal × Rate/100 × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the principal be 100p

Amount = 100p + 100p × 6/100 × Time 

⇒ 150p = 100p + 100p × 6/100 × Time

⇒ 150p - 100p = 6p × Time 

⇒ 50 = 6 × Time 

⇒ Time = 50/6 

⇒ Time = 25/3 years or 8 (1)/(3) {years}

**∴ The required time is 8 (1)/(3) years.**

• **Covalent Bond**

 
 
• When two atoms share one electron pair they are said to be joined by a single covalent bond.
 
• **In many compounds, we have multiple bonds between atoms. The formation of multiple bonds envisages the sharing of more than one electron pair between two atoms.**
 
• If two atoms share two pairs of electrons, the covalent bond between them is called a double bond. For example, in the carbon dioxide molecule, we have two double bonds between the carbon and oxygen atoms. Similarly in the ethene molecule, the two carbon atoms are joined by a double bond.

questions.question: Modern electrical generator works on _______ principle.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electromagnetic Induction**__.

__
 
• **The modern electrical generator works on the Electromagnetic Induction principle**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Faraday’s first law of electromagnetic induction** states that whenever a conductor is placed in a varying magnetic field, emf is induced which is called induced emf. If the conductor circuit is closed, the current will also circulate through the circuit and this current is called induced current.
 
• **Faraday's second law of electromagnetic induction** states that the magnitude of emf induced in the coil is equal to the rate of change of flux that linkages with the coil. The flux linkage of the coil is the product of a number of turns in the coil and flux associated with the coil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Electric generator function**-

 
 
• **​An Electric generator works on the principle of Faraday's law of Electromagnetic Induction.**
 
• An electric generator uses mechanical energy to generate electricity applying Faraday's law of induction.
 
• It spins a coil at a constant rate in a magnetic field to induce an oscillating emf.
 
• A conductor coil (a copper coil tightly wound onto a metal core) is rotated rapidly between the poles of a horseshoe-type magnet. The conductor coil along with its core is known as an armature.
 
• The armature is connected to a shaft of a mechanical energy source such as a motor and rotated.
 
• The mechanical energy required can be provided by engines operating on fuels such as diesel, petrol, natural gas, etc., or via renewable energy sources.
 
• When the coil rotates, it cuts the magnetic field which lies between the two poles of the magnet.
 
• The magnetic field will interfere with the electrons in the conductor to induce a flow of electric current inside it.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the weighted average formula to directly calculate the net gain.

Total Gain % = (Part₁ × Gain₁%) + (Part₂ × Gain₂%)

Total Gain % = (3/4 × 20%) + (1/4 × 15%)

Total Gain % = 15% + 3.75% = 18.75% ≈ 19%

**∴ The correct answer is 19%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fraction of stock sold at 20% gain = 3/4

Remaining fraction of stock = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4

Gain on the remaining stock = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Total Net Gain % = (Fraction₁ × Gain₁) + (Fraction₂ × Gain₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae100cebf80c6ce400de84143fd1af42923cd1dfd6499cf7dfd5dced049d7af9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total cost price (CP) of the stock be 400 units to make calculations easier.

⇒ CP of 3/4th of the stock = 3/4 × 400 = 300 units

⇒ CP of the remaining 1/4th of the stock = 1/4 × 400 = 100 units

⇒ Profit on the first part = 20% of 300 = (20 ÷ 100) × 300 = 60 units

⇒ Profit on the second part = 15% of 100 = (15 ÷ 100) × 100 = 15 units

⇒ Total Profit = 60 + 15 = 75 units

⇒ Total Gain % = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ Total Gain % = (75 ÷ 400) × 100

⇒ Total Gain % = 18.75%

⇒ Rounding off to the nearest integer, we get 19%.

**∴ The correct answer is 19%.**
